lines.text: She spent years hunting this dragon.
She should have looked closer.
It started on a rooftop, with a baby dragon and a torn, bleeding wing.
She carried it home, bandaged the wound, and named it Scales.
She taught it to fly.
Then one evening, a full-grown dragon dropped out of the sky,
snatched Scales in its claws, and was gone.
She didn't cry for long.
She took a blade and started walking.
Through deserts. Through bamboo forests. Through blizzards that nearly buried her.
Finally, an old shaman told her where the dragons nest.
Inside the cave, she found a baby dragon.
Then its parent found her.
It had her pinned. It could have finished her right there.
It hesitated.
She didn't.
The blade went in, and the dragon fell.
Then she saw the scar on its wing. The wing she had healed.
It was Scales.
And the face staring back from the pool of blood wasn't a girl's anymore.
